materials.title: Abstract
materials.body: Large language models are expensive to serve. We propose StepDistill, a method that trains a small student model on the intermediate reasoning steps of a large teacher, not only on final answers. On four reasoning benchmarks, a 1.3B student trained with StepDistill reaches 92% of the teacher's accuracy while being 50 times smaller. Gains are largest on math word problems and smallest on commonsense questions. We release code and data.

materials.title: Article: Machine learning code is only a small part of the system
materials.body: Many teams believe that the model is the hardest part of a machine learning product. In practice, the model code is often less than 10% of the system. The rest is data collection, feature pipelines, configuration, monitoring and serving. Each of these parts can create hidden technical debt. For example, a model may depend on a data source that another team changes without warning, or old experimental features may stay in production because nobody knows if they are still needed. The article suggests three habits: write down data dependencies, delete unused features regularly, and monitor model inputs, not only outputs. Teams that follow these habits spend less time fixing surprises and more time improving models.
